 Live updates: Jaylen Brown, Sixers host heated matchup with Celtics 
 Follow along for live updates as the Sixers host Jayson Tatum and the Celtics in a highly anticipated reunion. 
 By Eva Cheeseman • 
 Published 4 hours ago • 
 Updated 16 seconds ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 What to Know
 The East-leading Sixers (9-2) host the Celtics (8-2) for a highly anticipated reunion at XFinity Mobile Arena.
 Paul George makes his regular-season return to South Philly after he was traded to the Celtics for Jaylen Brown .
 Tension between Jayson Tatum and Brown has lingered since the trade as comments were made by both parties .
 Here's a full Sixers-Celtics preview with storylines and matchups to watch.
 Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (back) are both out for Tuesday night's matchup.
 Brown sidelined by foul trouble
 Jaylen Brown was whistled for his second foul at the 6:48 mark of the first quarter. The officials called him for a fast-break charge into Derrick White. Brown subbed out around a minute later and Dean Wade checked in. 
 It will be interesting to see how long Sixers head coach Nick Nurse waits before inserting Brown back into the game. On an intense, emotionally charged night for Brown against the team that traded him away this summer, will Nurse test whether can Brown play a lengthy stretch in the second quarter without picking up a third foul? Or will he take a more conservative approach with Brown's minutes? 
 Early whistles cut both ways
 Boston made seven of its first nine shots and led by as many as six points, but the Sixers remained close without matching that efficiency.
 The Celtics committed five team fouls before the first quarter’s midpoint, putting Philadelphia in the bonus. The Sixers made their first nine free throws, accounting for nine of their first 20 points.
 The whistle did not work entirely in Philadelphia’s favor. Jaylen Brown picked up two early fouls and went to the bench before the final five minutes of the quarter, cutting short his first shift against Boston.
 Brown left with four points and one assist. Jayson Tatum scored nine early points for the Celtics, while Tyrese Maxey countered with eight for the Sixers.
 Plenty of juice in the building 
 Anything involving Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum has led the home fans to amp up the volume in the opening minutes.
 Tatum and the Celtics have had the better start. The Celtics’ six-time All-Star has scored six early points to help Boston take an 18-12 lead. He got an easy layup when he used a back screen to break free from Brown.
 On the Sixers’ side, Tyrese Maxey was the only player to make a field goal in the first five or so minutes. He’s got eight of the team’s first 12 points. 
 J.B. is locked in 🔒
 Jaylen Brown warmed up for a heated matchup against a Sixers rival and his former team.
 Barlow rehabbing back injury
 Dominick Barlow did a light workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor about two hours before tip-off.
 On-court Dominick Barlow work:
— Noah Levick (@noahlevick.bsky.social) 2026-11-10T23:08:14.558Z 
 We’ll soon see where Barlow is able to progress to the next planned stage of his rehab. The 23-year-old forward hasn’t played yet this season because of an injury the Sixers have called a “lower back stress reaction."
 Last Wednesday, Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters that Barlow had seen a specialist and he expected it would be “another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear him for getting on the court to see where he is.”
